question: How is a skill door's EFFICACY measured when its match rate is saturated at 100%? intent, saveslate and sorted each show 100% match on the roster, which is equally consistent with a door that judges well and a door that never disagrees with anything put in front of it. The two are indistinguishable from the number, and the number is the only instrument the roster has.
whats_beyond: The roster measures USAGE (firings, refusals, findings, last fired) and calls the match-rate column efficacy. Refusals are counted — intent 6, saveslate 6, sorted 6 — so the doors DO refuse; what is unmeasured is whether a refusal, or an approval, was RIGHT. That needs a second opinion against the same packet, and there is no such instrument. Beyond here: whether efficacy at a door is measurable at all without a hand-judged sample, and if it needs one, who judges and how often.
source: decisions/2026-08-11-review-the-skills-and-workflow-monthly.json — review #1's `what_this_review_did_not_cover`, written as a caveat and left as prose. Filed as an open question on 2026-08-11 under decisions/2026-08-11-open-questions-land-with-cc-and-surface-at-the-hook.json, which rules that every such caveat ALWAYS becomes one.

resolved.answer: The answer shape is LLM periodic review of feedback to adjust gate parameters. The sieve measures deterministically; efficacy shows in the feedback the LLM reviews. This needs scheduled probes and LLM prompts for Hex to perform inspection evaluations — an intention with multiple sub-tickets, not a question.
